summary: Gorkem Yurtseven, co-founder and CTO of fal.ai—a self-described generative media platform—delivers a wide-ranging talk on the evolution and trajectory of generative media at the AI Engineer World's Fair. He begins with a personal anecdote about Sam Altman's DALL-E 2 tweets in April 2022, which he describes as a major turning point, and traces earlier precedents including Harold Cohen's computer-generated art, Google's Deep Dream, GANs, and the viral Prisma app. He notes the playing field leveled rapidly after DALL-E 2, with Midjourney launching as a Discord bot, Stable Diffusion open-sourcing models for consumer GPUs, and Flux arriving in summer 2024. Yurtseven distinguishes between marginal cost of creation (approaching zero) and marginal cost of creativity (still requiring human storytelling). He predicts generative media will transform social media, advertising, marketing, fashion, film, gaming, and e-commerce. He identifies advertising as the first industry to be impacted at scale, citing hyperpersonalized ads, on-the-fly generation, and interactive experiences, and references fal's A24 Civil War movie campaign where users generated personalized toy soldiers displayed in Times Square. E-commerce virtual try-on is highlighted as one of the clearest product-market fits in generative AI. On generative video, Yurtseven recalls the Sora announcement and shares fal platform revenue data: video usage grew from negligible in October 2024 to 18% by February 2025, and approximately 30% as of the talk date. He estimates video models are 20x more compute-intensive than image models and predicts the generative video market will be 100x to 250x larger than the image generation market. He mentions Google DeepMind's Veo 3 adding sound capabilities and anticipates future real-time video generation blurring the line between games and movies. In closing, Yurtseven notes image models continue to improve with Flux context and GPT-4o introducing new editing and text rendering capabilities, opening more enterprise use cases as mature industry players adopt these technologies. He announces fal is hiring machine learning engineers, inference engineers, and product engineers, and invites attendees to connect.

sections.title: Introduction to Generative Media
sections.summary: Yurtseven introduces fal.ai as a generative media platform handling video, audio, and image models via its inference engine, partnering with closed-source providers. He frames the talk as covering the history, present state, and future of generative media.

sections.title: Evolution of Generative Image Models
sections.summary: Yurtseven recounts the DALL-E 2 moment in April 2022, earlier attempts at computer-generated art (Harold Cohen, GANs, Deep Dream, Prisma), and the rapid leveling of the playing field as Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, and Flux democratized access. He argues marginal cost of creation is approaching zero while creativity and storytelling remain essential.

sections.title: Impact on Industries
sections.summary: Yurtseven predicts generative media will transform social media, advertising, marketing, fashion, film, gaming, and e-commerce. He identifies advertising as the first industry to be impacted at scale through hyperpersonalized, on-the-fly, and interactive ads, citing the A24 Civil War toy soldier campaign. He highlights e-commerce virtual try-on as one of the clearest product-market fits in generative AI.

sections.title: The Rise of Generative Video
sections.summary: Yurtseven compares the Sora announcement to the DALL-E 2 moment, shares fal platform data showing video usage growing from negligible to 18% to approximately 30%, and predicts the generative video market will be 100x-250x larger than the image market, citing 20x greater compute intensity and broader industry applicability.

sections.title: Future of Generative Media
sections.summary: Yurtseven discusses Veo 3's sound capabilities unlocking new use cases, and envisions future real-time video generation where one second of video is generated in one second, enabling streaming interactive content that blurs the line between games and movies.

sections.title: Conclusion and Call to Action
sections.summary: Yurtseven notes image models continue to improve with Flux context and GPT-4o adding new editing and text rendering capabilities, opening more enterprise use cases as mature industry players adopt these technologies. He announces fal is hiring ML, inference, and product engineers and invites attendees to connect and discuss generative media.
